location.text: An effect that doubles the quantities on your sheet doubles cards within each entry;

change_assessments.basis: Braintrust doubles quantities, not draw-panel entries. RR29 draws the indicated number from any one deck; RR29.1 excludes already-drawn types. Melange has three separate General lines, so doubled quantities mean two cards per line from three types. This is an ordinary application of the printed quantity and General rules.

change_assessments.change: Claim timing versus discard cost; Floyd retention

location.text: Claiming does not discard the asset unless an instruction requires it.

change_assessments.basis: Claim places the asset faceup; discarding requires an instruction. Floyd prints a draw trigger and persistent hand-size increase with no discard instruction. Revised text correctly distinguishes him from assets printing explicit discard-to-resolve text.

change_assessments.change: Aaron other-player proposal costs versus own costs and support cleanup

location.text: Proposal-cost discards are separate from support cleanup.

change_assessments.basis: Aaron applies when another player discards cards to propose a counteroffer. His controller's own payment and support cleanup do not match that condition. RR16.3 describes proposal costs; RR16.5 separately discards played deal cards.

change_assessments.change: Normal active-player hand check after End of Turn abilities

location.text: Only the active player makes the normal hand-size check, after their End of Turn asset abilities.

change_assessments.basis: RR3.3 explicitly orders active-player End of Turn abilities, hand check, then passing the token. RR16.5 deal cleanup has no hand check; RR30.2 checks at the end of the player's own turn. Printed exemptions remain controlling. Revision02's corrected Player Reference remains unchanged.

change_assessments.change: Units versus tokens and card-specific district/stage allocation

location.text: Units are the plastic Human First, orgcrime and prisec components.

change_assessments.basis: The official component list distinguishes the three unit types from android/illness/outage tokens. Spin Doctors specifies one stage in up to two districts; Ruthless Tactics specifies one stage in two districts; Sweeps Week expressly permits up to four stages in any districts. The added paragraph preserves those allocations. RR68.10 leaves stable unrest after outage removal. No Arrest Orders timing or unavailable-prisec outcome is supplied.

change_assessments.change: One unrest stage is one adjacent track position

location.text: Count one position along this track for each stage changed.

change_assessments.basis: RR68.1–68.2 defines adjacent state changes; stable to strike is two stages. The section retains ordinary caps and the specific Human First outage exception.

change_assessments.change: Event movement cascades and stopping after Root return

location.text: an enemy returned to the reserve has no further on-board movement, even if the event instructed it to move twice.

change_assessments.basis: RR35.1 continues movement until legal placement or the Root; RR35.2 then returns the component to reserve and adds two threat. RR35.0 moves from an occupied/attempted district, while RR48 defines reserve pieces as unused. An already-returned unit has no board district from which to make a second movement. Activist Cells Awaken does not place it back. This is an ordinary consequence of leaving the board, not a new stack/timing rule.

location.text: If theirs is strictly greater, you may steal 1 random hand card from them; equal capital does not qualify.

change_assessments.basis: Lily prints more capital than you, which excludes equality. RR6.6 places start-of-turn asset triggers before Refresh. No new exhaust cost or trigger is introduced.

change_assessments.change: Elizabeth original resolving player chooses the consequence

location.text: then you, the player who used her, choose whether that recipient must discard 3 actions or draw 3 actions of their sheet's topmost type.

change_assessments.basis: Printed Elizabeth instructs the resolving player to give the card, then choose the recipient's consequence. Giving the card does not transfer that in-progress instruction to the recipient. This retains the printed chooser and outcome.

change_assessments.change: All nine End of Turn rows label once per own turn

location.text: “End of Turn” means the owner's end-of-turn opportunity, once per ability.

change_assessments.basis: RR6.3, RR22.1–22.4 and RR66.2 limit these abilities to their controller's End of Turn at most once per ability. They remain optional via shared asset and turn rules. Receiving a new End of Turn asset during the step remains covered by the detailed turn text. Labels change no printed effects, payment or consequences.

result.factual_explanation: All changed text is supported by primary sources and ordinary applications. No new factual defect or affected remaining contradiction was found. Unchanged supported text retains original complete-audit and revision02 evidence.
result.scope_explanation: Arrest Orders interaction with generic prisec displacement and unavailable placement still lacks verified publisher clarification or accepted human interpretation. No SG01 ruling is adopted.

unsupported_ambiguity_limits.title: Arrest Orders versus ordinary prisec displacement and unavailable placement

summary_location.text: | Security — Arrest Orders | Place 1 prisec in any district to remove all other units in that district. |

unsupported_ambiguity_limits.supported_text: The summary accurately preserves the printed Arrest Orders instruction. It also accurately describes ordinary prisec protection as movement, not removal.
unsupported_ambiguity_limits.unresolved: The assigned printed sources do not establish the timing/priority that decides whether Arrest Orders removes other units before ordinary prisec placement forces enemy displacement, nor a definitive consequence for the removal clause when the prisec cannot be placed because none are available or another prisec occupies the district. No verified publisher clarification or accepted human interpretation is assigned; no proposed owner ruling is adopted.

primary_citations.coverage: complete FAQ inspected; no Arrest Orders ruling

scope_claim_location.text: This summary covers the complete base game and normal complete setup.

unsupported_ambiguity_limits.consequence: Cannot certify complete-core-scope readiness from these sources. The unsupported branch is an authority gap, not evidence that the literal Arrest Orders row is wrong. The summary's complete-base-game scope claim is unqualified despite this gap.

No revival of a superseded or canceled counteroffer inferred.
No owner ruling treated as adopted.
